title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: Scope of a Notice and Its Registration
content:
Under `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims`, a notice of loss concerns one container and one loss, and the cover's state at the time of lodging decides whether the notice goes on file.

## One container, one loss

A notice names a single container and a single loss. Where a further loss turns up in another container of the shipment, it is never folded into a claim file the cover already holds; it calls for a notice of its own.

## Going on file

Three lodging conditions govern registration:

- the claimant is a party the tier admits;
- the claims the cover has taken are still fewer than the tier's ceiling; and
- no claim is open on the cover.

Where all three are met, the notice is put on file, and the likelihood that it will be rejected once it is there does not count against it. Where any one of them fails, the notice does not go on file.

## Open claims

A claim file whose documents are still outstanding is an open claim. A claim ceases to be open when it is decided, or when the claimant withdraws it.

## Point of judgement (hypothetical)

- *Water damage is found in two containers of one delivered shipment.* Each container needs its own notice; the second loss is not written into the first claim file.
